item.title: Citations Made of Invisible Characters
item.description: How Suzent ties each claim in an answer to the page, file or search result it came from: source ids assigned by tools, Private Use Area markers the model copies, a parser that forgives messy models, and plain-text fallbacks for every place a badge can't go.

item.title: Long Conversations Without the Wait: How Suzent Compacts Context
item.description: When a long conversation outgrows the context window, most agents stop, re-read everything at full price, and make you wait for a summary. Suzent writes that summary from the prompt cache, prepares it in the background, and knows when the cache has gone cold.

item.title: Reach Your Agent From Anywhere, Through a Relay You Own
item.description: Suzent now lets your phone reach the agent on your computer from any network, with no VPN and no port forwarding, through a relay you deploy yourself. There is no Suzent cloud in the middle, and phone traffic is end-to-end encrypted.

item.title: Suzent is now on the Microsoft Store
item.description: Suzent's Windows desktop app is now on the Microsoft Store: one click to install, updates through the Store, and the same agent and data as before.

item.title: What Is Regent? Suzent's Orchestration Layer
item.description: Why your AI setup shouldn't turn you into a full-time dispatcher: how Regent acts as a single point of attention across autonomous project sessions, and how it differs from sub-agents.

item.title: Your Agent, or Theirs?
item.description: Personal agents went mainstream in 2026. Six big vendors now sell an always-on assistant that knows you increasingly well. Here is the quiet trade at the center of every one of them — and the question only you can answer.

item.title: Swap the Model, Keep the Agent
item.description: Why a sovereign AI agent's identity lives in its memory, skills, and workspace rather than in the model — and what has to be true architecturally for a model swap to be a config change.

item.title: What Happens to Your AI Agent When the Provider Shuts Down
item.description: Model deprecations, price changes, and product sunsets are routine. What you actually lose depends entirely on which side of the boundary your agent's memory and configuration live.

item.title: How to Own Your AI Agent's Memory
item.description: Agent memory you cannot read, edit, or move is not yours. What ownable memory looks like in practice, and how Suzent keeps it as Markdown on your own disk.

item.title: Sovereign AI Agent vs Cloud AI Assistant
item.description: An honest comparison of a sovereign AI agent and a hosted cloud AI assistant: what each one owns, what each one costs you, and when the rented option is the right call.

item.title: Sovereign AI for Individuals, Not Nations
item.description: The phrase sovereign AI usually means state-controlled models and compute. The same idea applies at the scale of one person, and that is what a sovereign AI agent is.

item.title: Suzent Mesh: A Nervous System for Your Sovereign AI
